title: Where to Buy Watches Online in Pakistan
summary: Where to buy watches online in Pakistan: five channels compared, original vs copy, the specs that matter, and the COD and warranty rules.
body_markdown:
Watches sell online in Pakistan through five channels: authorised dealers and brand stores, large marketplaces, Instagram and WhatsApp watch pages, reseller and wholesale platforms, and cross-border apps shipping from China. They differ on price, on what you are actually being sold, and on whether anyone stands behind the watch a month later.


Before you pick a channel, settle one question: are you buying an original branded watch, an unbranded watch that simply tells the time and looks good, or a copy of a famous design? All three are sold openly online here, often on the same page, and the price gap between them is enormous. Most disappointed buyers thought they were getting the first and paid for the second.


Below: what each channel is good at, the specifications that decide whether a watch is worth its price, how to size one from a photograph, and the reseller version of the same question.


## The five places to buy watches online in Pakistan


Match the channel to the tier you are buying. An authorised dealer is the wrong place to buy a PKR 2,000 fashion watch, and a social page is the wrong place to buy a watch with a warranty card that has to mean something.


### 1. Authorised dealers and brand stores


Every watch brand with a real presence in Pakistan sells through named authorised dealers, and increasingly through their own online store. This is the only channel where a serial number, an international warranty and a service path all exist together.


You pay full retail. What retail buys you is a watch that can be serviced, a movement that is what the brand says it is, and a resale value that survives. For anything bought as a gift or a milestone purchase, that is the whole point of the transaction.


**Best for:** branded originals, gifts, anything you expect to keep for years.


### 2. Large marketplaces


Marketplaces carry the widest watch catalogue and the widest quality range inside it. The same case design appears under a dozen seller names, sometimes as an unbranded fashion watch and sometimes with a famous name printed on the dial for a price no original ever sells at.


Read the seller's history rather than the product rating, and look for buyer photos — those are the only images shot on real stock. If you are weighing the big marketplaces against each other on price, payment and delivery, our comparison of the[best Daraz alternative in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/best-daraz-alternative-in-pakistan) covers how the options differ.


**Best for:** unbranded fashion watches, straps, watch boxes, tools, and sealed stock from long-established sellers.


### 3. Instagram and WhatsApp watch pages


Watch selling on social platforms is large, competitive and unevenly honest. The good pages photograph their own stock, film the watch running, and answer specification questions properly. The rest post the manufacturer's render and hope.


Rules that make this channel workable: insist on cash on delivery, ask for a video of the actual unit with the second hand moving and the caseback visible, and ask directly whether the watch is original, unbranded or a copy. A seller who answers that question plainly is one worth buying from.


**Best for:** niche and imported models, one-off pieces, sellers you have bought from before.


### 4. Reseller and wholesale platforms


These are built for people buying stock rather than buying a watch. Prices sit at a reseller tier instead of a retail tier, catalogues are organised by category rather than by brand, and the platform handles delivery and cash collection. Markaz sits here — browse the[product categories](https://www.markaz.app/shop/categories) to see how watches sit alongside the rest of the fashion-accessory range, check[current deals](https://www.markaz.app/shop/deals) for what is discounted this week, and look through the[supplier list](https://www.markaz.app/shop/supplier/list) to see who is actually behind the stock.


Ordinary buyers use it too, because the price sits below retail. The trade-off is that listings are written for sellers: less styling, more specification — which, for watches, is the more useful way round.


**Best for:** buying several pieces, gifting season, and anyone buying to resell.


### 5. Cross-border apps shipping from China


Cross-border apps carry the lowest sticker prices on unbranded and fashion watches, plus most of the smart-watch catalogue sold in Pakistan under many different names. The cost is time and uncertainty: long transit, customs handling that varies, and a return path rarely worth using from here.

If you want the same China catalogue with the import handled for you,[Markaz China categories](https://www.markaz.app/china/categories) land in about 10–17 days on cash on delivery, with no minimum order.


**Best for:** unbranded fashion watches, smart watches, straps and accessories.


## Original, unbranded or copy — know which one you are buying


This is the single most useful thing to understand before spending money on a watch online in Pakistan. Three different products share the same listing photos.


- **Original branded watches.** Sold by authorised dealers with a serial number, a warranty card filled in by the dealer, and a service centre. Priced accordingly. A famous Swiss name at a few thousand rupees is not one of these, whatever the listing says.
- **Unbranded and fashion-brand watches.** The largest part of the market. An honest quartz watch with a decent case, a name that is nobody's luxury brand, and a price that reflects what it is. Nothing wrong with them — the good ones look far better than they cost.
- **Copies of famous designs.** Sold under labels like "first copy" or "master copy". They carry someone else's name and someone else's trademark, they cannot be serviced, and if you resell them you are the one carrying that risk rather than the seller upstream.


The practical rule: if a listing uses a luxury brand's name, the price is the giveaway. If a listing uses no brand name at all, judge it purely on the specifications below — which is a much easier thing to do well.


## The specs that actually decide a watch


Watch listings hide behind adjectives. These are the numbers that mean something, and a seller who holds real stock can supply all of them.


- **Case diameter, in millimetres.** The one measurement that decides how it looks on you. Roughly 36–40 mm suits most wrists; 42–46 mm is a deliberately large watch. A listing that will not state the diameter is a listing to skip.
- **Lug-to-lug length.** Measured across the case from one strap horn to the other. This decides whether a watch overhangs a slim wrist, and it matters more than diameter on a small wrist.
- **Movement.** Quartz runs on a battery, keeps better time and costs less to own. Automatic winds from your wrist motion, has the sweeping second hand people like, and needs servicing eventually. Neither is better — they are different purchases.
- **Water resistance, read honestly.** "30 m" or 3 ATM means splashes and rain, not swimming. 5 ATM is fine for hand washing and light swimming; 10 ATM and above is a swimming watch. Nothing in this range means "shower with it daily" for a cheap watch, because the gaskets are the part they save money on.
- **Crystal.** Mineral glass scratches; sapphire mostly does not. On an everyday watch this is the difference between one that still looks new next year and one that does not.
- **Strap width and material.** Width in millimetres tells you whether you can replace the strap later. Genuine leather, synthetic and steel all age differently — steel survives Pakistani summers best, leather least.
- **Battery type.** For a quartz watch, ask which cell it takes. It costs almost nothing to replace if the cell is a common one, and rather more if it is not.

## Smart watches are a different purchase


Most smart watches sold online in Pakistan are the same handful of designs under many names. That is not automatically a problem — the price reflects it — but the checks are different from a mechanical or quartz watch.


Ask which phone operating systems the companion app supports, and what the app is called. Ask whether the strap uses a standard width so you can replace it. Treat headline battery claims as optimistic and assume real use is shorter. Check the IP or ATM rating rather than the words "waterproof". And be sceptical of any listing that borrows a famous smart-watch product name with a number after it.


Buy this category from a seller with a return path, because the failure mode is not cosmetic — it is a watch that will not pair. Much of the same advice applies to the rest of the gadget shelf; our guide on[where to buy mobile accessories online in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/where-to-buy-mobile-accessories-online-in-pakistan) covers the specification traps in more depth.


## Sizing a watch from a photograph


Wrist shots are shot on the wrist that flatters the watch. Work from your own measurement instead.


Wrap a tape measure — or a strip of paper you then measure — around your wrist just past the bone. That circumference is your number. As a rough guide, a slimmer wrist wears a 36–40 mm case comfortably, and a broader wrist carries 42 mm and up. Then check the lug-to-lug figure: if it is longer than the flat top of your wrist, the watch will sit awkwardly no matter how good the diameter looks.


For a steel bracelet, ask whether links can be removed and whether the seller does it before dispatch. For a leather or silicone strap, ask for the length of both halves and the hole spacing. A strap that is one hole too big is a watch you stop wearing.


## Cash on delivery, warranty and returns


COD is the default for online shopping in Pakistan and it is the main thing protecting a first-time watch buyer — you are not paying for something that never arrives. But COD only protects you up to the doorstep. Once you have paid the rider, you are inside whatever return policy the seller runs.


Do the inspection at the door, in this order: the glass and case for scratches, the second hand actually moving, the crown and pushers turning, the strap for its full set of links or holes, and the box for a warranty card and serial number if one was promised. That takes a minute and settles most disputes before they start.


Two things to confirm before ordering. Whether the courier allows you to open the parcel before paying, which varies by courier and by seller. And the return window in writing. ## Red flags on a watch listing


- **A luxury brand name at a fashion-watch price.** The most common misunderstanding in this category, and the easiest to avoid.
- **No case diameter anywhere in the listing.** Every real seller knows it. Its absence usually means the listing was copied.
- **"Waterproof" with no rating.** The word is doing work the specification cannot support.
- **Only a render, never a photograph.** Renders hide finishing quality — the exact thing that separates a good cheap watch from a bad one.
- **Advance payment demanded on a first order.** On a market where COD is normal, insisting on a transfer is a choice the seller is making for a reason.
- **A warranty promised only in the chat.** If the card is not in the box with a dealer stamp, treat the warranty as decoration.


## Buying watches to resell, not to wear


If you are buying stock rather than a watch, the question changes. You need a price you can mark up, stock you do not have to buy in bulk, and a delivery promise you can repeat to a customer.


Retail channels do not work for this. An authorised dealer sells at the price your customer could pay directly, and a marketplace listing is visible to that customer too. What works is a reseller-tier catalogue: order at supplier pricing, list at your own price, and let the platform deliver and collect the cash. ## A routine that works


Decide the tier first — original, unbranded or copy — because it decides the channel. Measure your wrist once and write the number down. Ask the seller for case diameter, lug-to-lug, movement and water-resistance rating; skip any listing where those cannot be supplied. Confirm the return window in writing. Then inspect the glass, the second hand and the strap at the door before you pay.


That takes a few minutes and removes most of what goes wrong with buying a watch from a photograph.


## Frequently asked questions


### Where is the cheapest place to buy watches online in Pakistan?


On sticker price, cross-border apps shipping from China. On price you can use this week, reseller and wholesale platforms sit below the retail markup while still delivering locally. Marketplaces fall in between and vary seller by seller. Authorised dealers are the most expensive, and for an original branded watch they are the only sensible option.


### How can I tell if a watch sold online is original?


Price first — an original branded watch does not sell for a small fraction of its retail price, no matter what the listing claims. Then the paperwork: a serial number, a warranty card stamped by a named dealer, and a service path. If a seller cannot produce those, treat the watch as unbranded and judge it on its specifications instead.


### What size watch should I buy?


Measure your wrist circumference with a tape or a strip of paper. A slimmer wrist generally suits a 36–40 mm case, a broader wrist 42 mm and up. Check the lug-to-lug measurement too — a watch longer than the flat part of your wrist will overhang regardless of its diameter.


### Is 30m water resistance enough for swimming?


No. 30 m (3 ATM) covers rain and splashes only. 5 ATM handles hand washing and light swimming, and 10 ATM and above is a genuine swimming watch. On inexpensive watches, treat every rating conservatively, because gaskets are where cost is saved.


### Can I return a watch bought with cash on delivery?


Within the seller's return window, and provided you have not damaged it. Inspect the glass, the movement and the strap at the door before you pay — that is when a problem is easiest to settle. Markaz orders run a 7-day return window on cash on delivery.


### Are watches a good product to resell in Pakistan?


They work well: no size matrix, small parcels, strong photographs, and demand that rises around gifting occasions. Start narrow with a few designs, describe them honestly, and pack for the glass. On a no-minimum platform like Markaz you can list first and order the unit once it sells.
